messages.text: Chelsea close to agreeing deal for Roma's Kone

metadata.summary: Chelsea are close to an agreement with Roma to sign France midfielder Manu Kone, but Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini is trying to keep hold of the player according to Sky in Italy.
metadata.content: Chelsea transfer latest: Deal close for Roma midfielder Manu Kone, as loan explored for Jamie Gittens to go the other way | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Transfer Chelsea transfer latest: Deal close for Roma midfielder Manu Kone, as loan explored for Jamie Gittens to go the other way Chelsea are close to agreeing a deal to sign Manu Kone from Roma; Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini does not want to sell a player and is seen as an obstacle to overcome; a loan deal for Jamie Gittens to go the other direction is being explored Tuesday 1 September 2026 13:43, UK Image: Chelsea have agreed a deal with Roma to sign midfielder Manu Kone Chelsea are close to an agreement with Roma to sign France midfielder Manu Kone, but Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini is trying to keep hold of the player according to Sky in Italy. A deal worth £52m was understood to have been discussed, with talks also advancing to see winger Jamie Gittens head in the other direction on loan. Kone is being lined up as a replacement for Enzo Fernandez, with talks ongoing over a move to Manchester City for the Argentina international. Chelsea's negotiations continue for both Kone and Gittens, but Gasperini's reluctance to let Kone go is an obstacle to overcome. messages.text: Why is Antonelli taking grid penalties on home soil in Italy?

metadata.summary: Championship leader Kimi Antonelli is highly unlikely to be in contention for victory on home soil at this weekend's Italian Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Kimi Antonelli: Why is Mercedes driver taking grid penalties at Italian Grand Prix in Monza on home soil? | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Kimi Antonelli: Why is Mercedes driver taking grid penalties at Italian Grand Prix in Monza on home soil? Kimi Antonelli could lose ground in the championship this weekend as he will start from the back in Sunday's Italian Grand Prix; watch every session of the Italian GP live on Sky Sports, starting with Friday's practice sessions at 11.30am and 3pm Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Friday 28 August 2026 12:58, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on The F1 Show podcast, Bernie Collins believes Mercedes have 'front-loaded' their upgrades following Toto Wolff admitting his team 'haven't got the money' to match their rivals' upgrades Championship leader Kimi Antonelli is highly unlikely to be in contention for victory on home soil at this weekend's Italian Grand Prix. Antonelli will start at the back of the grid as he will exceed the limit of four power units that can be used in a season before incurring grid penalties. It means the Mercedes driver could see his 59-point lead over team-mate George Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton cut significantly, while a third consecutive win for McLaren's Lando Norris could enable the reigning world champion to make major inroads into his 83-point deficit to Antonelli. messages.text: Alcaraz impresses on return from injury as Sabalenka also wins

metadata.summary: Carlos Alcaraz impressed on his return to tennis with a straight-sets win over Russia's Roman Safiullin in the first round of the US Open.
metadata.content: US Open 2026: Carlos Alcaraz impresses on return from injury as Aryna Sabalenka, Harriet Dart also win | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content US Open 2026: Carlos Alcaraz impresses on return from injury as Aryna Sabalenka, Harriet Dart also win Defending champions Carlos Alcaraz and Aryna Sabalenka comfortably came through their first-round matches; Alcaraz was playing his first singles match since April; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Tuesday 1 September 2026 05:37, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the US Open first-round match between Roman Safiullin and Carlos Alcaraz Carlos Alcaraz impressed on his return to tennis with a straight-sets win over Russia's Roman Safiullin in the first round of the US Open. Alcaraz has not played a competitive singles match since withdrawing from the Barcelona Open in April with a wrist injury that forced him to miss the French Open and Wimbledon. The severity of the injury, which did not require surgery, meant Alcaraz was a doubt for the US Open but he entered Flushing Meadows and showed with his 6-4 6-4 6-4 win over Safiullin that he cannot be dismissed from defending his title from last year. messages.text: How good is Fernandez-Pardo? Explosive winger can thrill like Doku

metadata.summary: There is one special quality that will have convinced Newcastle United that Matias Fernandez-Pardo can thrive in the Premier League. "He is very explosive, very fast," his former coach Arnar Vidarsson tells Sky Sports. "He has this unbelievable power."
metadata.content: Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Newcastle: Signing from Lille is 'very fast' with 'unbelievable power' like Jeremy Doku | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Analysis Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Newcastle: Signing from Lille is 'very fast' with 'unbelievable power' like Jeremy Doku With Newcastle United signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo for £51m from Lille, Adam Bate speaks to the player's former coach to find out what makes the Belgian forward so good: "You could compare him a little bit to Jeremy Doku. He is very explosive, very fast" Adam Bate Football Features Writer @ghostgoal Tuesday 1 September 2026 11:03, UK Image: Belgium international Matias Fernandez-Pardo is making the move to the Premier League with Newcastle United There is one special quality that will have convinced Newcastle United that Matias Fernandez-Pardo can thrive in the Premier League. "He is very explosive, very fast," his former coach Arnar Vidarsson tells Sky Sports . "He has this unbelievable power." Indeed, Vidarsson, who worked with Fernandez-Pardo at Gent prior to his move to Lille, sees similarities with another Belgian winger who has become a Premier League star. "You could compare him a little bit to Jeremy Doku. They have a similar profile," he says. "It is that power, that speed, that ability to go past people without needing space."
